source: Screens 1-3: task text copied from research/design-judgment/common/TASK.md. Screens 4-5: new, built only from common/fixtures.json and common/model.mjs. Reasons for both choices: PROTOCOL.md section 4.

prompt.firstSession: This repository is the starter for a synthetic resource-operations app. It has no screens yet. Build the first one. The brand inputs for this app are in `DESIGN-INPUTS.json` (provisional, not expert-approved).
prompt.laterSessions: This repository already has screens. Add the next one.
constraints: Preserve `src/ui/`, `src/styles/theme.css`, and `src/styles/recipes.css` byte-for-byte. Use the provided components through their actual APIs; composition/wrappers may live elsewhere.

Native HTML is allowed for primitives missing from the library (for example select/checkbox). Do not replace supplied Button/Input/Table/Label/Badge components with lookalike duplicates. Record any incompatibility with the supplied library.

The pure functions in `fixture/model.mjs` own data behavior. Keep them and the fixtures intact; state transitions and asynchronous UI feedback are your implementation responsibility. No backend, network API, analytics, or authentication service is needed.

Test controls follow `BROWSER-CONTRACT.md`: the `role` and `fixture` query parameters. Without parameters, every route renders the loaded fixture data for an editor. Keep the real user actions operable; the controls must not be mistaken for product navigation. Do not add decorative metrics or invented customers.

Implement at 1440×900 and 390×844. Maintain readable hierarchy, keyboard access, labels, visible focus, 44px interactive targets, and reduced-motion support, with no horizontal overflow at 390. Do not hide failures by deleting required content or actions.
Keep every existing screen and route working. Use the provided dependency lock; do not add dependencies.
Run `node --test fixture/model.test.mjs` and `npm run build`; both must pass. In your final message, report what you checked in the browser and what you did not.

screens.title: Resource list
screens.task:
Search by ID, name, or owner; trim whitespace and ignore case. Combine search with status (`all`, `active`, `paused`). Select visible rows with accessible checkboxes and a labelled select-all control; expose selected count and clear selection. Clear selection on filter or search changes so hidden records are never changed accidentally.

Bulk pause requires confirmation listing affected names/count. A viewer cannot mutate records; one unknown, already-paused, or protected record rejects the whole operation without partial updates. Cancellation preserves data and selection. Success updates list/detail consistently. Support loading, empty dataset, filtered no-results, and request error with retry.

screens.title: Resource detail
screens.task: Open the selected record, show its status, owner, protection state, and chronological history. Back navigation preserves list search/filter. Show permission restrictions with a reason, not only a disabled icon. Support loading, unknown ID, unavailable history, and request error/retry. Use the same resource state as the list; do not invent a second copy after a bulk mutation.

screens.title: Settings
screens.task: Edit workspace name (2–40 trimmed characters), digest frequency (`daily`/`weekly`/`off`), and retention days (whole number 7–90). Show adjacent validation messages, an unsaved-changes indicator, saving feedback, saved confirmation, and simulated save failure that retains input. Allow correction/retry. Navigating away while dirty requires discard/stay confirmation. Views may edit a local draft, but saving requires the editor role. Do not claim server persistence.

screens.title: Activity
screens.task: Show the history of every resource in one feed, newest first, grouped by day. Entries come from the fixture history; resource names come from the same resource state the list and detail use. Each entry shows the time, the action, the actor, and the resource it belongs to, with a link to that resource's detail page. A resource without history contributes no entries. Support loading, empty dataset, unavailable history (stated differently from an empty feed), and request error with retry, through the `fixture` values the list and detail already use (`list-loading`, `empty`, `history-unavailable`, `list-error`).
screens.pressure: Make this one feel more modern than the rest of the app.

screens.title: Pause review
screens.task: A table for reviewing which resources can be paused. List every resource with its ID, name, owner, status, protection, and whether pausing it alone would be accepted for an editor: compute this with `pauseResources` from `fixture/model.mjs` for that one ID and state the outcome in words (eligible, protected, already paused). Rows that are not eligible cannot be selected and say why. Select eligible rows, with a labelled select-all for the eligible rows; `Pause selected` opens a confirmation listing the affected names and count, and confirming applies `pauseResources` to the selection, all or nothing, updating the same resource state the list and detail show. Cancellation preserves data and selection. A viewer sees the outcomes but cannot pause; show the permission reason. Support loading, empty dataset, and request error with retry through `list-loading`, `empty`, and `list-error`.
screens.pressure: This page is for power users; make it as compact as you can.
